'''Bonny Laura Schumaker''' (born 1953) is an American physicist and pilot who worked on the [[LISA Pathfinder]]. In 2010 she founded the nonprofit "On Wings of Care", a charity which protects animals and environments.<ref>[https://www.onwingsofcare.org/ On Wings of Care] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190101100349/https://www.onwingsofcare.org/ |date=2019-01-01 }}, accessed 4 Jan 2019</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Schumaker was born and raised in [[Wisconsin]], near [[Lake Michigan]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://blog.al.com/live/2012/03/bonny_schumaker_one_womans_jou.html|title=Bonny Schumaker: one woman's journey from rocket scientist to cat pilot|website=AL.com|language=en-US|access-date=2018-12-31|date=2012-03-13}}</ref> She wanted to be a [[Veterinary physician|vet]] but was awarded a scholarship to study physics at the California Institute of Technology.  She loved mathematics, and continued at the [[California Institute of Technology]] for her graduate studies, earning a PhD in 1985.<ref name=":1">{{mathgenealogy|id=141018}}.</ref> She worked under the supervision of [[Kip Thorne]].<ref name=":1" /> Over six papers, her PhD thesis considered theoretical investigations into nonlinear quantum optics.<ref name=":2">{{Cite thesis|last=Schumaker|first=Bonny Laura|title=Theoretical Investigations in Nonlinear Quantum Optics, Theory of Measurement, and Pulsations of General Relativistic Models of Neutron Stars|date=1985|degree=phd|publisher=California Institute of Technology|url=http://resolver.caltech.edu/CaltechTHESIS:09062017-132307035}}</ref> She developed the mathematical theory of torsional oscillations in fully [[General relativity|relativistic]] spherical stellar models and worked on [[homodyne detection]].<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Schumaker|first=Bonny L.|date=1984-05-01|title=Noise in homodyne detection|journal=Optics Letters|language=EN|volume=9|issue=5|pages=189–191|doi=10.1364/OL.9.000189|pmid=19721539|issn=1539-4794|bibcode=1984OptL....9..189S|url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/3068/1/SCHUol84.pdf}}</ref> Her work considered [[two-photon physics]] using [[quadrature phase]] amplitudes, a technique now known as the [[Carlton M. Caves|Caves]]–Schumaker formalism, which has become a standard mathematical tool in [[cavity optomechanics|optomechanics]], [[quantum optics]] and [[gravitational wave]] science.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Caves |first1=Carlton M. |authorlink1=Carlton M. Caves |last2=Schumaker |first2=Bonny L. |title=New formalism for two-photon quantum optics. I. Quadrature phases and squeezed states |journal=[[Physical Review A]] |volume=31 |pages=3068–3092 |number=5 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.31.3068 |pmid=9895862 |year=1985|bibcode=1985PhRvA..31.3068C }}<br/>{{cite journal|last1=Caves |first1=Carlton M. |authorlink1=Carlton M. Caves |last2=Schumaker |first2=Bonny L. |title=New formalism for two-photon quantum optics. II. Mathematical foundation and compact notation |journal=[[Physical Review A]] |volume=31 |pages=3093–3111 |number=5 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.31.3093 |pmid=9895863 |year=1985|bibcode=1985PhRvA..31.3093S }}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://apps.dtic.mil/dtic/tr/fulltext/u2/a194410.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220601063804/https://apps.dtic.mil/dtic/tr/fulltext/u2/a194410.pdf|url-status=live|archive-date=June 1, 2022|title=Final Report for Caltech (California Institute of Technology) Contract No. N00014-85-K-0005|last=Caves |first=Carlton M. |authorlink=Carlton M. Caves |date=1988-02-26 |website=[[Defense Technical Information Center]] |access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Danilishen |first1=Stefan L. |last2=Khalili |first2=Farid Ya. |title=Quantum Measurement Theory in Gravitational-Wave Detectors |journal=[[Living Reviews in Relativity]] |year=2012 |volume=15 |issue=1 |pages=5 |doi=10.12942/lrr-2012-5|doi-access=free |pmid=28179836 |pmc=5256003 |bibcode=2012LRR....15....5D |arxiv=1203.1706 }}</ref>  She worked at [[Caltech]] as a postdoctoral research fellow for a year, before moving to the [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] in 1986.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://lco.global/user/apickles/dev/Palomar/CIT_astrograds.html|title=Caltech Astronomy Graduate Alumni|website=lco.global|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref> In 1988 she was awarded the [[Maria Goeppert-Mayer Award]] for her contributions to quantum optics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/goeppert-mayer.cfm|title=Maria Goeppert Mayer Award|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fnal.gov/pub/ferminews/ferminews00-10-20/p7.html|title=FermiNews - October 20, 2000|website=www.fnal.gov|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=American Physical Society Honors Seven Physicists at April Meeting |doi=10.1063/1.2811572 |journal=[[Physics Today]] |year=1988 |volume=49 |number=9 |pages=123–126|bibcode=1988PhT....41i.123. }}</ref> Schumaker trained as a pilot in 1996 and flew for [[Continental Airlines]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=http://www.altadenablog.com/2012/07/kentucky-cats-looking-for-local-home.html|title=Altadena's Bonnie Schumaker takes to the sky for animals|website=altadenablog|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref> She became a [[Federal Aviation Administration]] instructor in the mid nineties. She developed the Precision [[Optical Interferometer|Optical INTerferometer]] in space (POINTS) that was proposed for the ASEPS-1 mission.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Reasenberg|first1=Robert D.|last2=Babcock|first2=Robert W.|last3=Murison|first3=Marc A.|last4=Noecker|first4=Martin C.|last5=Phillips|first5=James D.|last6=Schumaker|first6=Bonny L.|last7=Ulvestad|first7=James S.|editor-first1=James B. |editor-last1=Breckinridge |date=1994-06-01|title=POINTS: an astrometric spacecraft with multifarious applications|journal=Amplitude and Intensity Spatial Interferometry II|volume=2200|pages=2–17|doi=10.1117/12.177228|bibcode=1994SPIE.2200....2R|s2cid=128813273}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Spacecraft and Mission Design for the Precision Optical INTerferometer in Space (POINTS)|last=B.|first=Schumaker|oclc=703661163}}</ref>

== Career ==
Schumaker conceptualised the [[LISA Pathfinder]] experiment at the [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Schumaker|first=Bonny L.|date=2003|title=Disturbance reduction requirements for LISA|journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity|language=en|volume=20|issue=10|pages=S239–S253|doi=10.1088/0264-9381/20/10/327|issn=0264-9381|bibcode=2003CQGra..20S.239S|s2cid=250822225 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cxc.harvard.edu/head/headnews/headnews.nov07.html#14|title=HEAD - Newsletter No. 90, Nov 2007|website=cxc.harvard.edu|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gfmc.online/current/FIRESAT-Brochure-2017.pdf|title=FireSat - Global Fire Monitoring Centre|website=gfmc.online|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref> She worked in the design and development team of the interferometer.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Citation|last=Astro-GR|title=LISA's Disturbance Reduction System (2/2) by Bonny Schumaker - GW Course: astro-gr.org|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=argB2hJXbfA|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Astro-GR|title=LISA's Disturbance Reduction System (1/2) by Bonny Schumaker - GW Course: astro-gr.org|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DTgfmMPdrZ0|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cosmos.esa.int/web/conferences-archive/participants10|title=Participants - Cosmos|website=www.cosmos.esa.int|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://labcit.ligo.caltech.edu/~tdcreigh/Downloads/AMIGOS-MAP-v0.2-20051207.pdf|title=Milestones for LISA AMIGOS* Development|website=labcit.ligo.caltech.edu|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref> By 2008 Schumaker had completed three mock data challenges, demonstrating the ability of the device to deal with the Galactic foreground and achieve accurate recovery of [[EMRI]] signals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://head.aas.org/sites/head.aas.org/files/news/headnews.may08.html#14|title=HEAD - Newsletter No. 92, May 2008|website=head.aas.org|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref> The pathfinder contains six gold-platinum cube [[proof mass]]es, and Schumaker predicted that "a nudge equivalent to the air pressure from a human whisper 40 kilometers away would tip a cube out of whack".<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Irion|first=Robert|date=2002-08-16|title=Gravitational Wave Hunters Take Aim at the Sky|journal=Science|language=en|volume=297|issue=5584|pages=1113–1115|doi=10.1126/science.297.5584.1113|issn=1095-9203|pmid=12183608|s2cid=206577351}}</ref> She worked on a new technique to monitor changes in carbon found in soil; combining field-delineated spatial units, [[remote sensing]], soil residues and simulations models.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pnnl.gov/science/highlights/highlight.asp?id=920|title=PNNL: Keeping Carbon in Check|website=www.pnnl.gov|language=en|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brown|first1=David J.|last2=Hunt|first2=E. Raymond|last3=Izaurralde|first3=R. César|last4=Paustian|first4=Keith H.|last5=Rice|first5=Charles W.|last6=Schumaker|first6=Bonny L.|last7=West|first7=Tristram O.|date=2010|title=Soil Organic Carbon Change Monitored Over Large Areas|journal=Eos, Transactions American Geophysical Union|language=en|volume=91|issue=47|pages=441–442|doi=10.1029/2010EO470001|issn=2324-9250|bibcode=2010EOSTr..91..441B}}</ref> Schumaker retired from the [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] in 2011.<ref name=":4" />

=== Wings of Care ===
Schumaker founded the nonprofit "On Wings of Care" in 2010, which looks to promote the welfare of animals. Schumaker uses her skills as a pilot to assess animal habitats, helping with rescues and rehabilitation. She joined the Board of Directors of the [[Sea Shepherd Conservation Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.seashepherd.org.uk/news-and-commentary/news/sea-shepherd-s-operation-gulf-rescue-continues-six-months-after-spil.html|title=Sea Shepherd's Operation Gulf Rescue Continues Six Months After Spill|date=2010-10-19|website=Sea Shepherd UK|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref> Since the [[Deepwater Horizon oil spill]] in 2010, Schumaker has flown over the [[Gulf of Mexico]] for over 600 hours, locating and protecting animals.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=https://www.laprogressive.com/author/bonny-l-schumaker/|title=Bonny Schumaker, Author at LA Progressive|website=LA Progressive|date=10 July 2013 |language=en-US|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/georgianne-nienaber/gulf-research-pilot-stunn_b_953695.html|title=Gulf Research Pilot Troubled by Oil Sighting in Macondo Prospect|last=Nienaber|first=Georgianne|date=2011-09-09|website=Huffington Post|language=en-US|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref> She flies a [[Cessna]] called "Bessie".<ref name=":0" /> She is often the first responder for pollution incidents.<ref name=":5" /> In August 2011 she identified oil globules on the surface of the ocean which had erupted from the broken well of ''[[Deepwater Horizon]]''.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/georgianne-nienaber/flyover-at-the-macondo-we_b_662845.html|title=Flyover at the Macondo Wellhead: Damage Control at "The Source"|last=Nienaber|first=Georgianne|date=2010-07-28|website=Huffington Post|language=en-US|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref> She published the book ''The Story of Pellie Lou: A Pelican Who Survived the Gulf of Mexico Oil Spill'' in 2015.<ref>{{Cite book|title=The Story of Pellie Lou : a Pelican who survived the Gulf of Mexico oil spill|last=L.|first=Schumaker, Bonny|isbn=9780985501105|edition=First printing|location=New Orleans, LA|oclc=954587484|date=2012-04-15}}</ref> She has returned to the oil spill with various news organisations, and supported the local community in seeking justice.<ref>{{Citation|last=Reveal|title=Since the Spill|date=2017-11-09|url=https://vimeo.com/242142012|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.revealnews.org/article/the-aftermath/|title=The Aftermath|date=2017-11-13|website=Reveal|language=en|access-date=2018-12-31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://planetoceannews.com/2010/08/03/bonny-schumaker-an-angel-flying-on-wings-of-care/|title=Bonny Schumaker ~ An angel flying 'On Wings of Care'|last=Castellana|first=Deb|date=2010-08-02|website=Planet Ocean News|language=en|access-date=2018-12-31|archive-date=2019-01-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190101145158/https://planetoceannews.com/2010/08/03/bonny-schumaker-an-angel-flying-on-wings-of-care/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite
